patterns: how do i write a cover letter
entries.answer: A cover letter is a short page explaining why you are the right person for one specific job, and its job is the opposite of a resume's. A resume lists what you have done; the cover letter argues why that matters here, in a paragraph rather than a list, and it is read before the resume by whoever is shortlisting. The part that decides it is usually the first line, because a letter that opens by explaining why the company is famous shows the reader has not yet made the connection to themselves. The second is specificity: a claim supported by a concrete thing you did beats an adjective about yourself, and "I reduced the queue by a third" is doing work that "I am hardworking" is not. In the Philippines it is also common to be asked for one even when applying online, and a two-page essay about your life story is the standard failure. Keep it short enough to be read in under a minute.

patterns: how to prepare for an interview
how to answer tell me about yourself
entries.answer: An interview is a test of whether working with you will be manageable, and it is worth treating it that way rather than as a test of knowledge, because the knowledge a job needs is usually learnable and the part people have to assess is harder to change. Preparation that actually helps is specific: knowing what the company does, having two or three questions ready, and being able to say honestly why you want the work. The most common failure is reciting a prepared answer, because the interviewer can tell, and the second most common is having no questions at all, which reads as no interest rather than as nerves. A useful technique is to treat an answer as an explanation out loud, in the middle of a story, rather than a list of attributes, because an explanation can be followed and a list can only be judged. Salary is legitimately asked about, and asking what the range for the role is is less awkward than naming a figure first.
